newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tung urges Hong Kong to become less politicised.
newsitem.headline: Tung urges Hong Kong to become less politicised.

text.p: Hong Kong's chief-executive designate Tung Chee-hwa urged Hong Kong people on Friday to focus less on politics after the territory's handover to China.

"I really hope that after the handover on July 1, 1997 that our society will not be as politicised and we can focus more on livelihood issues such as housing, education and welfare," Tung said in message to mark the Lunar Year of the Ox.
"I hope that we can all work together to create a caring society that has a strong social fabric," Tung said.
Tung urged Hong Kong people to respect Chinese traditions that stress harmony, compassion and family values.
"When we Chinese speak of 'The Doctrine of the Equilibrium' we mean not to go to the extremes," he said.
But Tung also said that Hong Kong people "should combine the best of the East and the West and find our way forward."
Hong Kong reverts to China on July 1 after more than 150 years of British rule.
Tung, who was born in the Year of the Ox, said he hoped that people would recognise in him the Ox's virtues of industry, sincerity and perseverance.
